articles.title: Four T. rex footprints hint at how fast it traveled
articles.snippet: Though poorly preserved, the prints suggest the dino ambled at 1.6 meters per second, roughly the speed of a human walking briskly.
articles.summary: Four poorly preserved Tyrannosaurus rex footprints suggest the dinosaur moved at a speed of 1.6 meters per second. This speed is roughly equal to a human walking briskly.

articles.snippet: Thanks to one of these events in 1977, astronomers discovered Uranus's rings.

articles.title: Mystery solved? Why ‘sleeping’ ants suddenly explode with activity
articles.snippet: For decades, scientists have puzzled over what triggers some colonies of ants to burst from rest into community-wide action. Math may now explain this.
